earlier_scan.source_named: Only Wittmann 1991 classification note in Glottolog; no phonological description of Tijuana Sign Language found (word stress not applicable to sign modality in any located source).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mexican Sign Language' (citing Faurot, Dellinger, Eatough & Parkhurst 2001 [1992], The identity of Mexican sign as a language)
sources.note: No mention of Tijuana or of prosody/stress; only that LSM shows regional variation (80–90% lexical similarity across Mexico).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Spurious languages', section 'Removed from Ethnologue, 12th ed., 1992'
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Row reads verbatim: "Tijuana Sign Language (Mexico) [TJS] – added to Ethnologue 1988 by mistake due to a misunderstanding, removed in 1992. No evidence that it ever existed."

sources.citation: Wittmann, Henri. 1991. Classification linguistique des langues signées non vocalement. Revue québécoise de linguistique théorique et appliquée 10(1): 215-288.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only mention of Tijuana in the whole article is Annexe I, p. 285, entry 75: "75. TJS. Sans date/R? Tijuana Sign Language. Prototype. Tijuana (Mexique). Prototype-R?" — a one-line classification-list entry (code / first attestation / name / immediate filiation / location / ultimate filiation), compiled from the Ethnologue 11th-ed. database (fn. 35, p. 248). No description, no prosody, no phonology anywhere in the article for this entry.
